name: Zophar
overview: Zophar is a male figure identified as the Naamathite and recognized as one of the friends of Job. Beyond this unique attribute, Scripture does not provide additional personal details such as his tribal affiliation or other distinguishing notes. His role is primarily connected to his association with Job during the trials described in the Book of Job.
namesAndTitles: The name Zophar is a proper name possibly meaning 'peep' or 'twitter,' akin to the sound made by a bird. This meaning, while noted, is not explicitly connected to his character or actions in Scripture. The name was not given by God but is simply his personal designation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Zophar beyond his friendship with Job. There are no listed relatives or additional relational information provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Zophar's significance in the biblical narrative stems from his role as one of Job's three friends who come to comfort and counsel him during his suffering. As the Naamathite friend, he contributes to the dialogues that explore themes of suffering, righteousness, and divine justice. His presence helps frame the theological discussions central to the Book of Job.
